answer: Collateral is slashed jointly when correlated behavioural faults fire inside the same window. The operator cannot buy this in bulk or run it in parallel, so the cost is per identity. The river is the collateral at risk, the quartz the behavioural signature that groups identities, and the ledge the joint forfeiture that punishes the group: splitting into many quartz groups avoids the joint loss but scatters the river into smaller, individually useless stakes.
